body.translated_text: Anaparāddhastotra (Hymn to the Faultless One) of <s>Mātṛceṭa</s> (metre: <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>, incomplete; Hartmann 1988: p. 74 ff.; text reconstruction here includes the fragment Hoernle 149/250 (=British Library, Or. 15009/149) not yet available to Hartmann)

body.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x t karmaṇyatām āhṛtāḥ || 10
body.translated_text: [...] ... [...] were brought to industriousness. || 10

children.text: kaḥ kasyānuśayasya bhe x x x x x x ryavaiśeṣiko
children.translated_text: Who, of which latent tendency, [could know] the distinction [...] [...]

children.text: yo yasmiṃ pravibhajya vi x x x x x x kabhedas tvayā |
children.translated_text: who, distinguishing in which [being] [...] [...] the division [of things was taught] by you? |

children.text: ko vā tatra tathā tathā k. x dadhat siddhiṃ na saṃprāptavāṃ
children.translated_text: Or who, thus and thus [...] holding, did not attain success?

children.text: jijñāsāpi na ced ihāsty. y. x x x x x x x x x || 11
children.translated_text: If there is not even the desire to know here [...] [...] [...] || 11

children.text: x x syāśubhayā dayāpar. c. y. x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [...] with compassion, devoted to compassion [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x mānayoḥ pravicayādvaidhāpathājñānayoḥ |
children.translated_text: [...] through the investigation of honor and [...], of the dual-path and of ignorance; |

children.text: dṛṣṭīnām api śu x x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: of views too, the purification [...] [...] [...]

children.text: x x x vihitāvadh. x x x x x x x x x x x || 12
children.translated_text: [...] having established the limit [...] [...] [...] || 12

children.text: yan nādhīḥ śamatho ratho 'ditimirā dṛṣṭiḥ purāssāriṇī
children.translated_text: Whose study is <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), whose chariot is free from the darkness [of ignorance], whose vision is the forerunner,

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x |
x x x x x vagraho nirupadhā x x varaḥ sādhanaṃ
children.translated_text: [...] grasping, without attachment [...] the best means

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ digapajñ. x x x x x x .opadeṣṭā svayam || 13
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the direction [...] [...] the teacher himself. || 13

children.text: yānaṃ sa x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: The vehicle [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x .ābhivivṛto diṅ nirbhayā darśitā |
children.translated_text: [...] surrounded by [...], the fearless direction was shown; |

children.text: dattaṃ panthy. x x x x x x x yaṃ sandarśi x x x nāṃ
children.translated_text: the path was given [...] [...] shown to beings [...],

children.text: niryātuṃ yadi n. x x x x x x x rya. kim anyat tvayā || 14
children.translated_text: if not to lead [them] out [...] [...] what else [was done] by you? || 14

children.text: kaḥ kāṃkṣāṃ kva ca x x yasya bhavatā nāpākṛtaḥ saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Who had longing, and where [...] whose doubt was not removed by you?

children.text: kas te śāsanam āśṛto 'tana x x x x x nān muktavān |
children.translated_text: Who, resorting to your teaching, [...] [...] did not attain liberation? |

children.text: kaḥ śakyaḥ pathi saṃniyoktu x x x x .y. si nānugrahaṃ
children.translated_text: Who could be set upon the path [...] [...] you do not [withhold] your grace;

children.text: kiṃ tad bhūtam adarśi yaṃ na bahuśo x x x x x x x || 15
children.translated_text: what being was seen that was not repeatedly [...] [...] || 15

children.text: ko 'rthitvaṃ tava dharmam abhyupagato ya x x x x x x
children.translated_text: Who, having approached you for your <s>dharma</s>, [...] [...]?

children.text: ko vā kasya gu x sya bhājanam abhūd yasmiṃ sa nāpāditaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or who was the vessel of which virtue [...] in whom it was not accomplished? |

children.text: kasyābhitva x x x x x x x x x x x x x l. kṛthāḥ
prāpte vā ka upe x x x x x x lokānta x x pi te || 16
children.translated_text: or who, having arrived [...] [...] even to the ends of the world [...] || 16

children.text: x ṣāṃ cit svayam [a]bhy[u]pety[a] k[a]thitaṃ ke cic cir. x rpitā
children.translated_text: [...] to some, having approached [them] himself, it was told; some were long [...] established;

children.text: x x x x x x x x x t. mirās tatraiva ke cit kṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: [...] [...] some were made [...] free from darkness right there; |

children.text: āya x x x x x x x x x x x x x .ātrīkṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: coming [...] [...] [...] were made [...];

children.text: prabhraṣṭeṣv a x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x || 17
children.translated_text: for those who had fallen [...] [...] [...] || 17

children.text: x tithyaṃ kṛ x x m uttamadhanair abhyāgatebhya x x
children.translated_text: [...] hospitality [...] to those who had arrived with the highest wealth [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x sukhaṃ bhavyo x x x x x |
x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x
x x x x x x k. to manasi te dharmadhvajā bh. x x || 18
children.translated_text: [...] [...] established in your mind, the banner of <s>Dharma</s> [...] || 18

children.text: x x x x m upetya ye 'py upa x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [...] having approached [...] those who also [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x |
x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x x
x x x śaraṇāḥ śaraṇyaśara x x x x x x x x || 19
children.translated_text: [...] those who take refuge, O worthy of refuge [...] [...] || 19

children.text: x x x x x x x kāram aśaṭho x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [...] [...] action, without deceit [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x x .y. pagamair dharmāy. x x x x |
children.translated_text: [...] [...] through approaches [...] for the sake of <s>Dharma</s> [...]; |

children.text: netre vṛṣṭam abh. x x x x kh. v.ḥ saddharma x x x x
children.translated_text: upon the eyes was rained [...] [...] the true <s>Dharma</s> [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x .āḥ saddharmam ud. x x x || 20
x x x x x x tmane vidadhatā kiṃ strījano varjito
children.translated_text: [...] for one who provides for himself — were women excluded?

children.text: yūnaḥ sthāpayitā śive 'dhvani bahiḥ kiṃ bālavṛddhāḥ kṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: In establishing youths on the auspicious path — were the old and children left out? |

children.text: prasvasthā[n u]pakarṣatā parihṛtāḥ kiṃ kṣiptamattāturās
children.translated_text: In uplifting the healthy — were the deranged, intoxicated, and sick disregarded?

children.text: tat kiṃ v antaram asti yatra na ca te sūkṣmaḥ praviṣṭo nayaḥ || 21
children.translated_text: What then is that interval where your subtle guidance has not entered? || 21

children.text: kiṃ x .āsv api x x taṃ na x x raṃ māyāsu māyāvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Was it not [...] even in [...] — in illusions, [you] the master of illusions?

children.text: kiṃ vīryaṃ prati nāntadoṣarahitas tantrīnayo varṇitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Regarding valor — was not the method of practice (<s>tantrīnaya</s>) described, free from the fault of [wrong] end? |

children.text: kiṃ kālā manaso na niśrayaśamopekṣāśrayā deśitā
children.translated_text: Were not the times of the mind taught as resting in cessation, equanimity, and their supports?

children.text: labhya tvā kim akurvatā na tu jagad yuktaṃ tvayā śreyasā || 22
children.translated_text: Having obtained you, what did the world not do? Indeed, you have endowed it with the highest good. || 22

children.text: doṣā[nve]ṣaṇa x x x x x x x x .e guṇānveṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Searching for faults [...] [...] searching for virtues;

children.text: kiṃ pāpāya samudyateṣu satataṃ na tvaṃ hitāyodyataḥ |
children.translated_text: when [beings] are constantly engaged in evil, are you not always striving for their benefit? |

children.text: supte jāgarikāṃ kim a x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: For the sleeping, wakefulness [...] [...]

children.text: kiṃ khinno 'si ja[na]sya nāsya vinayāyānāthakeśagrahāt || 23
children.translated_text: were you wearied by seizing [beings] by the hair of their indiscipline, like [caring for] orphans, for their training? || 23

children.text: kiṃ sevāvamate j[an]e pi x .r.(?) x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: For those who despise service [...] [...] [...]

children.text: x x pt[ā] na jighāṃsavaḥ svasutavaṃ na svīkṛtā vyutthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: [...] were not the murderous ones, taken up like one's own sons, [turned from their] waywardness? |

children.text: kiṃ raudreṣu kṛpālutā na vivṛt[ā] j. .m. .u x x x x
children.translated_text: Was compassion not displayed toward the fierce? [...] [...]

children.text: x x x x x x x taṃ sad api te kiṃ taj jagad vakṣyati || 24
children.translated_text: [...] [...] what will the world say of that [deed] of yours, even [what is] true? || 24

children.text: sarvaṃ te suvicintitaṃ sucaritaṃ suvyāhṛtaṃ ca prabho
children.translated_text: All by you was well-considered, well-conducted, and well-spoken, O Lord;

children.text: sa
children.translated_text: and every glance of yours [...]

children.text: rvaṃ c[ai]va vilo[kanaṃ tava] x x [lo]kānukampāmayam |
children.translated_text: was filled with compassion for the world; |

children.text: dagdhās te kumatāndhakāravihatā ye te tiro 'vasthitā
children.translated_text: burned are those blinded by the darkness of wrong views, who stood against you;

children.text: ye tvā n[ātha]m apāśrit[ās] tu x x x mārasya te 'bhyunnatāḥ || 25
children.translated_text: those who did not resort to you as protector [...] were exalted by <s>Māra</s>. || 25

children.text: stutvā tvā yad upārjitaṃ jitakale satpuṇyapaṇyaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: By praising you, what has been earned by me, O conqueror of time, is the meritorious merchandise of the good;

children.text: tenāstūddhṛtajanmanirmama x x janmedam antyaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: by that, may [I be] freed from birth — selfless [...] may this be my final birth! |

children.text: saṃsāre nivasanti ye 'pi vidhṛtās tais tair vibandhair janā
children.translated_text: Those beings who dwell in <s>saṃsāra</s>, held by this and that bond —

children.text: mā ratnatraya[sa]ṃ[ś]rayakṣaṇam ṛte janmā[ni] teṣāṃ tv x x || 26
children.translated_text: may their births, except for the moment of resorting to the <s>Three Jewels</s>, [...] || 26

body.translated_text: The <s>Anaparāddhastotra</s> is complete — the work of the elder teacher <s>Mātṛceṭa</s>.

body.text:
Unknown Stotra (ms. found in Charkhlik at the southern route of the Silk Road,
script of the 4th/5th centuries; incomplete; Hartmann 1988: 90)
body.translated_text: Unknown Stotra (manuscript found in Charkhlik on the southern route of the Silk Road, script of the 4th/5th centuries; incomplete; Hartmann 1988: 90)

children.text: x ... [a]dbhutaguṇe tvayi kalyāṇacetasi |
children.translated_text: [...] in you of wondrous virtues, of benevolent mind, |

children.text: vikkriyāṃ nāspadaṃ lebhe yathā dh. ... ||
children.translated_text: alteration found no foothold, just as [...] ||

children.text: x+1 ... ṣṭate kaś cit tvayy asādhutvam eva tu |
children.translated_text: [...] someone [...] wickedness in you;

children.text: kṛpāyase 'dhikataraṃ mātevātmajam āturam ||
children.translated_text: you feel even greater compassion, like a mother for her sick child. ||

children.text: x+2 [paraduḥ]khānapekṣīdaṃ svaduḥkhaikāturaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: This world, heedless of others' suffering, is afflicted only by its own pain;

children.text: tvaṃ svaduḥkhāny anādṛtya paraduḥkhāturaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: you, disregarding your own sufferings, are always afflicted by others' pain. ||

children.text: x+3 ... duḥkhāni svaprāṇātivyayair api |
children.translated_text: [...] sufferings, even at the cost of your own life;

children.text: yā te prītir abhūt sādho sā teṣām api nābhavat ||
children.translated_text: the joy that was yours, O virtuous one, was not [felt by] them. ||

children.text: x+4 ... [lo]ko 'yaṃ na tathā pīḍyate yathā |
children.translated_text: [...] this world is not so afflicted as

children.text: kṛpāpeśalasaṃtānaḥ pīḍyase tvaṃ parārtibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you, whose continuum is tender with compassion, are afflicted by others' sufferings. ||

children.text: x+5 ... chatrau putre vānugrahāntaram |
children.translated_text: [...] toward an heir, or a son — there is no difference in grace,

children.text: kṛpāviṣṭamater akṣṇoḥ savyadakṣiṇayor iva ||
children.translated_text: for one whose mind is possessed by compassion, between the left and right eyes. ||

children.text: x+6 ... vahet mūrdhnā mune pādarajāṃsy api |
children.translated_text: [...] would bear upon his head even the dust of your feet, O sage,

children.text: karuṇānikaṣodgāri yasya te sarvvaceṣṭitaṃ ||
children.translated_text: whose every action pours forth [gold] on the touchstone of compassion. ||

children.text: x+7 ... khedyamāno 'pi cchidyamāno 'pi cāsakṛt |
children.translated_text: [...] though harassed, though cut again and again,

children.text: nāyāsīd vikkriyāṃ dhīra grahākkrānta ivoḍurāk ||
children.translated_text: your mind, O steadfast one, did not undergo alteration — like the moon seized by [the demon] <s>Rāhu</s>. ||

children.text: x+8 ... vyasanāvarte karuṇā satvavatsalā |
children.translated_text: [...] in the whirlpool of calamity, compassion, tender toward beings,

children.text: na tatyāja kṣaṇam api tvāṃ dharmān iva dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: did not abandon you even for a moment — like <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) [does not abandon] dharmas. ||

children.text: x+9 ... n[i]tyānubaddhaṃ ca tvāṃ doṣā akṣamādayaḥ |
children.translated_text: [...] and constantly attendant upon you, the faults of impatience and the rest

children.text: notsehire samāveṣṭuṃ ta ... ||
children.translated_text: were unable to envelop [you] [...] ||

body.text: Praṇāmastava (Gilgit finds, metre Mattamayūrī, incomplete; Hartmann 1997)
body.translated_text: <s>Praṇāmastava</s> (Hymn of Prostration) (Gilgit finds, metre <s>Mattamayūrī</s>, incomplete; Hartmann 1997)

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x x
x x x x x x x x x x x x x |
x x x x x (viciki)tsātimiraghnaṃ
children.translated_text: [...] the destroyer of the darkness of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>),

children.text: cakre mūrdhnā taṃ jinasūryaṃ praṇamāmi ||
children.translated_text: I bow my head to that Sun among <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors). ||

children.text: x+1 gambhīratvād apy upati x x x x ḥ
children.translated_text: Though profound, [his teaching] [...] [...]

children.text: x myāgrāṇāṃ saṃkalitāni skhalitāni |
children.translated_text: [...] the stumbles of the foremost [...] were collected; |

children.text: svākhyātatvād apy upateruś ca yuva ḥ
children.translated_text: though well-expounded, the young ones fell [into error];

children.text: x x x x x mitam atyadbhutabuddhim ||
children.translated_text: [...] [...] the one of exceedingly wondrous intelligence. ||

children.text: x+2 kas taṃ mūrdhnā vādivariṣṭhaṃ na namasyet
children.translated_text: Who would not bow his head to that foremost of teachers,

children.text: svākhyātatvāt sā[garaga]mbhīratarārtham |
children.translated_text: whose meaning, by its well-expounded nature, is deeper than the ocean? |

children.text: adyājñātaṃ yasya mataṃ dvyaṅguladhībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Whose doctrine is unknown today by those of two-finger[-breadth] intelligence,

children.text: kleśāveśakṣipra x x x pramadābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: [those] women swiftly [...] by the possession of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). ||

children.text: x+3 mṛtyuskandhakleśasurākhyān iha mārān
children.translated_text: The <s>Māras</s> here called death, the aggregates, the afflictions, and the devas —

children.text: kṣāntijñānātyantanirodhāstra x x ḥ |
children.translated_text: with the weapon of the complete cessation of patience and knowledge [...]; |

children.text: jigye sākṣād yaḥ sa tathājījapad anyān
children.translated_text: he who conquered them directly — he thus also caused others to conquer;

children.text: nābhyarcet taṃ ko 'vasitātmārthaparārtham ||
children.translated_text: who of resolute mind would not worship him, devoted to both his own and others' welfare? ||

children.text: x+4 ādīptānāṃ santa x x x x yakṛdbhir
children.translated_text: For blazing [...] compassionate-hearted ones,

children.text: yaḥ sattvānāṃ kleśamahāpāvakavegaiḥ |
children.translated_text: for beings [consumed] by the force of the great fire of afflictions; |

children.text: śāntiṃ cakre dharmaśivāmbuvyatisargais
children.translated_text: he who created peace by the outpouring of the auspicious waters of <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: taṃ vande ['haṃ] x x jalaughaṃ munimegham ||
children.translated_text: I venerate that sage-cloud, [...] a flood of water. ||

children.text: x+5 kāntāvaktrodvīkṣaṇadīkṣākṣaṇamagnaṃ
children.translated_text: [<s>Nanda</s>,] immersed in the initiation of gazing at a beloved's face,

children.text: mārasyājñā .i x x x [a]bhyupayātam |
children.translated_text: who had come under <s>Māra</s>'s command [...]; |

children.text: cakre nandaṃ yaḥ sa bhujiṣyaṃ śirasāhaṃ
children.translated_text: he who made <s>Nanda</s> a servant [of the Dharma] — I bow my head

children.text: vande yuktaṃ taṃ patitā x x x x ḥ ||
children.translated_text: to that one, the appropriate [guide] for those who have fallen [...] ||

children.text: x+6 deśādeśāveśavaśāt krodhahutāśa-
children.translated_text: Under the sway of regional customs, <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, who had entered

children.text: jvālāmālāmadhyagato yo 'ṅgulimālam |
children.translated_text: into the midst of the garland of flames of the fire of anger — |

children.text: kṣe x x x x x x x cchliṣṭanipātaṃ
children.translated_text: [...] [...] who had fallen into a tight embrace [with evil],

children.text: taṃ kāntārottāraṇadhuryaṃ praṇato 'ham ||
children.translated_text: to that one, the foremost in uplifting the beloved ones, I bow. ||

children.text: x+7 cakre gatvā śāntavanāntām urubilvāṃ
children.translated_text: He who, having gone to <s>Urubilvā</s>, the end of the peaceful forest,

children.text: keśakleśāpoddharaṇaṃ yo jatilānām |
children.translated_text: brought about the removal of the affliction of matted hair for the ascetics — |

children.text: tasmai siddhāyottamavidyādhararājñe
children.translated_text: to that accomplished supreme king of <s>vidyādharas</s>,

children.text: nānādṛṣṭikleśaviṣaghnāya namo 'stu ||
children.translated_text: the destroyer of the poison of the various wrong views and afflictions — homage! ||

children.text: x+8 ṛddhyā kāṃś cit kāṃś cid amoghair upadeśaiś
children.translated_text: Some through miraculous power, some through infallible teachings,

children.text: cittādeśaiḥ kāṃś cid upāyair aparaiś ca |
children.translated_text: some through reading minds, and others through various means — |

children.text: nānārūpair yaḥ sa vininye naradamyāṃs
children.translated_text: He who tamed those to be tamed among men by various forms,

children.text: taṃ vande 'haṃ lokamahāsārathim ekam ||
children.translated_text: I bow to him, the one great charioteer of the world.

children.text: x+9 tṛṣṇānadyāṃ doṣarayacchinnataṭāyāṃ
children.translated_text: [...] of those who have fallen into the river of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), whose banks are broken by the current of faults,

children.text: dṛṣṭigrāhānekabhayāyāṃ patitānām |
children.translated_text: which is full of many dangers from the crocodiles of wrong views—

children.text: prajñāhastaṃ yaṃ sa kṛpādīrgham ayacchat
children.translated_text: he who extended the hand of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), long with compassion,

children.text: taṃ trātāraṃ tārayitāraṃ praṇato 'ham ||
children.translated_text: to him, the protector, the deliverer, I bow down.

children.text: x+10 mithyājñānāveśavaśānām avaśānāṃ
children.translated_text: [...] of those who are powerless, under the sway of the possession of false knowledge,

children.text: janmāvartāviddhagatīnām agatīnām |
children.translated_text: of those without path, whose courses are driven into the whirlpool of births—

children.text: yaḥ sattvānāṃ niḥsaraṇopāyam apāya-
children.translated_text: he who, wishing their welfare, taught the means of escape to beings

children.text: prāgbhārāṇām āha hitaiṣī sa gatir me ||
children.translated_text: who are weighed down toward the lower realms—he is my refuge.

children.text: x+11 lokasyaivaṃ niṣpratikārān upakārāṃś
children.translated_text: [...] he who, having gone forth, rendered such benefits to the world without any possibility of return,

children.text: cakre gatvā yaḥ sa balātkārasuhṛttvam |
children.translated_text: attaining friendship by the force of his will—

children.text: mitraṃ nāthaṃ bāndhavam āryaṃ gurum īśaṃ
children.translated_text: friend, protector, kinsman, noble one, teacher, lord,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyas taṃ hy avitṛptah praṇamāmi ||
children.translated_text: to him, again and again, unsatiated, I bow down.

children.text: x+12 bhaktyāpārād buddhaguṇāmbhonidhimadhyād
children.translated_text: [...] from the boundless ocean of the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities, through devotion,

children.text: uddhṛtyemaṃ bindum avaikaṃ yad avāptam |
children.translated_text: having drawn up even this single drop, what has been obtained—

children.text: adyāsmābhiḥ puṇyam atas santu samāṃśāt
children.translated_text: by the merit now gained by us, may from an equal share

children.text: sarve sattvā dharmasatattvāmṛtabhājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all beings become vessels of the nectar of the true <s>dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: || <s>Praṇāmastava</s> (Hymn of Obeisance) ||
<s>Sattvārādhanastava</s> (metre: <s>Vasantatilakā</s>, <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>, <s>Mandākrāntā</s>; Lévi 1929)

children.text: 3 [sattvopa]kāram adhikṛtya gato 'smi siddhiṃ
children.translated_text: Having undertaken the welfare of beings, I have attained perfection;

children.text: sattvārtham eva tanum eṣa samudvahāmi |
children.translated_text: for the sake of beings alone I bear this body.

children.text: sattvān hinasti manasāpi hi yaḥ sa kasmān
children.translated_text: He who harms beings even in thought—why then

children.text: mām eva saṃśrayati yo mayi nirvyapekṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: does he resort to me, who is indifferent to me?

children.text: 4 pūjā tu sā bhavati sattvahitekṣaṇāpi
children.translated_text: That worship which produces satisfaction in the mind of the one to be worshipped,

children.text: pūjyasya yā mnasi tuṣṭim upādadāti |
children.translated_text: even mere regard for the welfare of beings, is true worship.

children.text: hiṃsātmikā paraviheṭhanasambhavā vā
children.translated_text: But worship that is of the nature of harm or arises from tormenting others,

children.text: pūjā na pūjyam anugacchati saṃskṛtāpi ||
children.translated_text: even if elaborately performed, does not follow the one to be worshipped.

children.text: 5 dārāḥ sutāś ca vibhavāś ca mahattvarājyaṃ
children.translated_text: Wives, sons, wealth, sovereignty and great power,

children.text: māṃsāni śoṇitavaśe nayane śarīram |
children.translated_text: flesh, blood, eyes, and body—

children.text: yeṣāṃ priyatvam adhikṛtya mayojjhitāni
children.translated_text: these I have abandoned for the sake of the dearness of those beings;

children.text: yas tān viheṭhayati tena viheṭhito 'ham ||
children.translated_text: he who torments them, by him I am tormented.

children.text: 6. sattvopakāraparamā hi mamāgrapūjā
children.translated_text: The highest worship of me is devotion to the welfare of beings,

children.text: sattvāpakāraparamaś ca parābhavaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: and the greatest degradation would be devotion to harming beings.

7 sattvān prāpya mayā kṛtāni kuśalāny ārādhitās tāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Through beings I performed meritorious deeds, propitiated the <s>Tathāgata</s>s,

children.text: prāptāḥ pāramitāś ca sattvasamiter evārtham ātiṣṭhatā |
children.translated_text: and attained the <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections), all while fulfilling the purpose of beings.

children.text: sattvārthena samudyatena manasā mārasya bhagnaṃ balam
children.translated_text: With a mind set upon the welfare of beings, the power of <s>Māra</s> was broken;

children.text: sattvair eva tathā tathā viracitaṃ yenāsmi buddhaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by beings in such and such ways was it brought about that I was made a <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: 8 kasmin vastuni sidhyatām iha kṛpā maitrī ca kvālambyatāṃ
children.translated_text: Toward what object should compassion be perfected here? And where should loving-kindness be cultivated?

children.text: kvopekṣāmuditādivastuviṣayāḥ kasmin vimokṣadayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where are the objects of equanimity, joy, and the other states? Toward whom are the deliverances of liberation?

children.text: kasyārthe karuṇāpareṇa manasā kṣāntiś ciram bhāvitā
children.translated_text: For whose sake was patience long cultivated with a compassionate mind?

children.text: na syur janmani janmani priyavidhau mitraṃ yadi prāṇinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If living beings were not dear friends in birth after birth, there would be none of these.

children.text: 9 sattvā eva gajādibhāvagatayo dattā mayānekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Beings themselves, taking the forms of elephants and other creatures, were given by me many times;

children.text: sattvā eva ca pātratām upagatā deyaṃ mayā grāhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: beings themselves became worthy recipients and accepted my gifts.

children.text: sattvair eva vicitrabhāvagamanād asmatkṛpā vardhitā
children.translated_text: Through beings, by going through various states of existence, my compassion was increased;

children.text: sattvān eva na pālayāmi yadi cet kasyārtham arthaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if I do not protect beings, then for whose sake was all this effort made?

children.text: 10 saṃsāre vyasanābhipātabahule na syur yadi prāṇino
children.translated_text: If in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which abounds in the onslaught of misfortunes, there were no living beings

children.text: janmāvartaviḍambanena yamalokaṃ prāpya sātmīkṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: who, tormented by the whirlpool of rebirths, have reached the realm of <s>Yama</s> and been consumed—

children.text: saṃsārāt taraṇaṃ ca saugatam idaṃ mahātmyam atyadbhutaṃ
children.translated_text: then this crossing of <s>saṃsāra</s>, this wondrous greatness of the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: kasyārthena samīhitaṃ yadi na me sattvā bhaveyuḥ priyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whose sake would it have been undertaken, if beings were not dear to me?

children.text: 11 yāvac cedaṃ jvalati jagataḥ śāsanaṃ śāsanaṃ me
children.translated_text: As long as this teaching of mine blazes forth for the world,

children.text: tāvat stheyaṃ parahitaparair ātmavadbhir bhavadbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: so long should you, who are devoted to the welfare of others and self-possessed, remain steadfast.

children.text: śrutvā śrutvā {ca?} mama vicaritaṃ sattvahetor akhinnaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard again and again of my conduct for the sake of beings, unwearied,

children.text: khedaḥ kāryo na ca tanum imām uktasārāṃ bhavadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you should not feel distress regarding this body whose essence has been declared.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Sattvārādhana</s> (Pleasing of Beings), a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtrānta</s>, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One.
"Epithets of the <s>Buddha</s>" (Schlingloff 1955: 82f.)

children.text: munaye lokanāthāya naravīrāya dhīmate |
children.translated_text: To the Sage, the lord of the world, the hero among men, the wise one,

children.text: sarvasattvāśayajñāya namas tasmai maharṣaye || 1
children.translated_text: the knower of the dispositions of all beings—homage to that great seer. || 1

children.text: yena dṛṣṭvā jagad idaṃ pradīptaṃ kleśavahinā |
children.translated_text: By whom, having seen this world ablaze with the fire of <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions),

children.text: śami
children.translated_text: it was quenched with the water of knowledge—homage to that well-wisher. || 2

children.text: taṃ jñānatoyena namas tasmai hitaiṣiṇe || 2
yasya na skhalitaṃ kiṃc[i]d [vā]kcharīramanomayam |
children.translated_text: He whose slightest fault of speech, body, or mind has never occurred—

children.text: sarvadoṣavimuktāya namo 'stv akliṣṭakarmaṇe || 3
children.translated_text: homage to him who is free from all faults, whose actions are undefiled. || 3

children.text: yas tīrṇo jñānabāhubhyāṃ vipulaṃ jñeyasāgaram |
children.translated_text: He who crossed the vast ocean of the knowable with the arms of knowledge—

children.text: namas tasmai narendrāya vikramātulabuddhaye || 4
children.translated_text: homage to that lord of men, of unequalled vigour and wisdom. || 4

children.text: yena kṛtsnam idaṃ jñeyaṃ dṛṣṭvā svamaticakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: By whom all this knowable was seen with the eye of his own insight—

children.text: sarvadharmavide tasmai namo 'stv amalacakṣuṣe || 5
children.translated_text: homage to that knower of all <s>dharma</s>s, of stainless vision. || 5

children.text: yaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ bhāgyarūpagoṇodbhavaiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is the foremost of all beings by fortune, form, and qualities—

children.text: dvipañcabaline tasmai namo 'stv aprativādine || 6
children.translated_text: homage to him of tenfold strength, the irrefutable one. || 6

children.text: vadhakāpatyayor yasya manas tulyaṃ pravartate |
children.translated_text: He whose mind proceeds equally toward the slayer and toward his own child—

children.text: svacittavaśine tasmai vimalāyārhate namaḥ || 7
children.translated_text: homage to that stainless <s>arhat</s>, master of his own mind. || 7

children.text: yo bhittvā jñānatuṇḍena mohāṇḍaṃ niḥsṛtaḥ svayam |
children.translated_text: He who, having pierced the egg of delusion with the beak of knowledge, emerged by himself—

children.text: gurave muktasaṅghāya namas tasmai svyaṃbhuve || 8
children.translated_text: homage to that teacher, free from all attachment, the self-born one. || 8

children.text: nirgṛhītendriyā x x [jñ]āna[g]ocaracāri[ṇe] |
children.translated_text: To him whose senses are restrained, [...] who moves in the domain of knowledge,

children.text: maitrākāruṇyacittāya tas[m]ai guṇa[va]te namaḥ || 9
children.translated_text: whose mind is filled with loving-kindness and compassion—homage to that virtuous one. || 9

children.text: brahmendravaruṇ[ādi]tyayakṣāsuranaroragaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Asura</s>s, men, and <s>Nāga</s>s—

children.text: y[aḥ] s[tu]taḥ pūjitaś cāpi namas tasmai yaśasvin[e] || 10
children.translated_text: he who is praised and worshipped—homage to that glorious one. || 10

children.text: x x satyāni catvāri dṛṣṭā x kāracakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: [...] the four truths seen [...] with the eye of [compassion?],

children.text: ta
children.translated_text: to him, [and to]

children.text: smai tac ca x x x x vi[śu]ddhamanase namaḥ || 11
children.translated_text: that [...] of purified mind, homage. || 11

children.text: viṣāgnisarpapratimaṃ yena kāmasukhaṃ ca x |
children.translated_text: By whom sensual pleasure, which is like poison, fire, and serpents, [was abandoned],

children.text: x x x x x x x x tasmai bhagava[te namaḥ] || 12
children.translated_text: [...] homage to that Blessed One. || 12

children.text: ā
children.translated_text: To the knower of dispositions and latent tendencies, the revealer of the path and the non-path,

children.text: śay[ā]nuśayajñāya mārgāmārgopadarśina |
nirmamāya niḥsaṅgāya tasmai śāntātmane namah || 13
children.translated_text: to him who is free from possessiveness, free from attachment, of peaceful self—homage. || 13

children.text: yasya rāgādibhir do[ṣ]air mano naivopalipyate |
children.translated_text: He whose mind is never stained by the faults of passion and the rest—

children.text: praśāntarajase tasmai śucine vaśine na[maḥ] || 14
children.translated_text: homage to him of calmed passion, the pure one, the self-controlled. || 14

children.text: tasmai śāntāya [ma]hate śāstratattvārthadarśine |
children.translated_text: To that peaceful, great one, the seer of the true meaning of the teaching,

children.text: gataye vītapāpāya namo 'stv asamaceta[se] || 15
children.translated_text: the refuge, free from sin—homage to him of unequalled mind. || 15

children.text: saṃ[s]kṛtaṃ ca x yuktaṃ ca pūrvamadhyāntaśobhanam |
children.translated_text: That which is well-formed and [...] fitting, beautiful in the beginning, middle, and end—

children.text: yo vadaty atulaṃ dharmaṃ tasmai matimate namaḥ || 16
children.translated_text: he who speaks the incomparable <s>dharma</s>—homage to that supremely wise one. || 16

children.text: kleśatrayavimuktāya trisamādhivihāriṇe |
children.translated_text: To him who is free from the three <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions), who abides in the three <s>samādhi</s>s,

children.text: lokatraya[v]im[u]ktāya nama[s ta]sm[ai] tricakṣuṣe || 17
children.translated_text: who is liberated from the three worlds—homage to him of the three eyes. || 17

children.text: śivāya śubhaśīlāya śākyaputrāya śrīmate |
children.translated_text: To the auspicious one, of pure conduct, the son of the <s>Śākya</s>s, the glorious one,

children.text: namaḥ śāntiṃ prayātāya śaraṇāya śamaiṣiṇe || 18
children.translated_text: homage to him who has attained peace, the refuge, the seeker of tranquillity. || 18

children.text: nirvṛtasyāpi yasyeha-m ājñā vartaty anākulā |
children.translated_text: He whose command continues untroubled in this world even after his <s>nirvāṇa</s>—

children.text: dharmarajñe namas tasmai sarvārthavaśavartine || 19
children.translated_text: homage to that king of <s>dharma</s>, the master who governs all purposes. || 19

children.text: yenendujvalanādityāḥ prabhayā niṣprabhīkṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: By whom the moon, fire, and sun were outshone in radiance—

children.text: namas tejasvine tasmai kāñcanojjvalamūrtaye || 20
children.translated_text: homage to that resplendent one, of golden, blazing form. || 20

children.text: sarvārthaguṇayuktāya sarvabhūtānukampine |
children.translated_text: To him who is endowed with all excellent qualities, who is compassionate toward all beings,

children.text: namaḥ sarvārthasiddhāya sarvasattvahitaiṣiṇe || 21
children.translated_text: homage to him by whom all aims are accomplished, who seeks the welfare of all beings. || 21

children.text: nānumānair na caupamyair nāśravair nānutarkitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Not by inference, nor by analogy, nor by testimony, nor by conjecture

children.text: guṇānto vidyate yasya namas tasmai mahātmane || 22
children.translated_text: can the limit of his virtues be found—homage to that great-souled one. || 22

children.text: caturthyā yad vibhaktyā me stutvā stutiśataiḥ stutam |
children.translated_text: By whatever merit has been obtained by me through praising with hundreds of praises, using the dative case,

children.text: puṇyaṃ tad astu sattvānāṃ catuḥsatyārthabuddhāye || 23
children.translated_text: may that be for the awakening of beings to the meaning of the four noble truths. || 23

body.translated_text: The <s>Munayastava</s> (Hymn to the Sage) is complete.
<s>Rāhulastava</s> (Schlingloff 1955: 89-92)

children.text: sattvasāra namas tubhyaṃ viśuddhātulabuddhaye |
children.translated_text: O essence of beings, homage to you, of pure and unequalled wisdom,

children.text: yas tvaṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu jagaddhitaparāyaṇaḥ || 1
children.translated_text: you who in all circumstances are devoted to the welfare of the world. || 1

children.text: yad ādau tava kāruṇyād uttitārayiṣor jagat |
children.translated_text: That at the beginning, out of your compassion, wishing to deliver the world,

children.text: vyavasāyaḥ samutpannas tad dhi sumahad adbhutam || 2
children.translated_text: a resolution arose—that indeed is most wonderfully great. || 2

children.text: yathaiva prathamaṃ cittam utpannaṃ tava bodhaye |
children.translated_text: Just as your first thought arose for the sake of awakening,

children.text: tvaṃ tathaivāsya lokasya pūjyaś copari ca sthitaḥ || 3
children.translated_text: even so you are worthy of worship by this world and are established above it. || 3

children.text: prapannāñ charaṇaṃ trātuṃ ceṣṭante kila sādhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: The virtuous strive to protect those who have taken refuge, it is said;

children.text: trātum abhyutthitas tu tvam aprapannam idaṃ jagat || 4
children.translated_text: but you rose up to protect this world that had not yet taken refuge. || 4

children.text: viśrutaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vyavasāyaṃ tavādbhutam |
children.translated_text: Your wondrous resolve, renowned in the three worlds —

children.text: śrotum apy ātmadaurbalyān nālam alpaguṇo janaḥ || 5
children.translated_text: a person of scant merit is not even able to hear of it, due to his own weakness. ||5||

children.text: parārthe niravekṣasya janasyātmaṃbharer iha |
children.translated_text: How will the heart of a person who is self-serving in this [world] be pleased

children.text: vyavasāye tavodāre prasatsyati kathaṃmanaḥ || 6
children.translated_text: with your noble resolve, [you] who have no regard for yourself in working for others' sake? ||6||

children.text: jīvaloko hy ayaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pṛthagāśayaceṣṭitaḥ |
children.translated_text: For this entire world of living beings, with its diverse inclinations and actions,

children.text: svasattvasadṛśaṃ karma vāñchaty anukaroti ca || 7
children.translated_text: desires and imitates only deeds that accord with its own nature. ||7||

children.text: svasattvasyānurūpaṃ tat kāruṇyasya ca te mune |
children.translated_text: In keeping with your own nature and your compassion, O Sage,

children.text: niścayaḥ prāg yad utpannas trātum ārtam idaṃ jagat || 8
children.translated_text: the resolve arose long ago to save this suffering world. ||8||

children.text: jānan saṃsāraduḥkhāni gantuṃ śakto 'pi nirvṛtim |
children.translated_text: Knowing the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, though able to go to <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation),

children.text: ciraṃ kliṣṭo 'si saṃsāre kāruṇyād eva kevalam || 9
children.translated_text: you endured suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for a long time — solely out of compassion. ||9||

children.text: suraloke nṛloke vā jātam anyatra vā kva cit |
children.translated_text: Whether born in the world of the gods, in the human world, or elsewhere —

children.text: karuṇā tvā na tatyāja mātā sutam ivaurasam || 10
children.translated_text: compassion did not abandon you, as a mother [does not abandon] her own son. ||10||

children.text: saṃsārasulabhair duḥkhair durvahair api pīḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though afflicted by the sufferings readily found in <s>saṃsāra</s>, hard to bear though they are,

children.text: svabandham iva saṃśliṣya niścayaṃ na mumocitha || 11
children.translated_text: you embraced [them] as if they were your own bonds and did not release your resolve. ||11||

children.text: yat kiṃ cid akaraḥ puṇyaṃ manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever merit you performed through actions of mind, speech, and body —

children.text: parān eva tad uddiśya kṛpālo kṛtavān asi || 12
children.translated_text: all of that, O Compassionate One, you did directing it toward others. ||12||

children.text: parakāryaṃ svakāryaṃ te paraduḥkhaṃ ca bādhakam |
children.translated_text: Others' work was your own work, and others' suffering was [felt as] your own affliction;

children.text: avīcir api ramyas te parānugrahakāmyayā || 13
children.translated_text: even <s>Avīci</s> [hell] was delightful to you, out of the desire to help others. ||13||

children.text: sādhor utsahamahatas tavātikaruṇātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: O Protector, through the great zeal of you, the virtuous one of supremely compassionate nature,

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ jagad idaṃ nātha kaḍatratvam upāgatam || 14
children.translated_text: this entire world has come under your protection [lit. become your wife]. ||14||

children.text: sarvalokena sarvajña yad duḥkham anubhūyate |
children.translated_text: O Omniscient One, whatever suffering is experienced by the entire world,

children.text: tad ātmani samāveśya tvaṃ cakartha ciraṃ śramam || 15
children.translated_text: drawing that into yourself, you labored for a long time. ||15||

body.translated_text: The world, pitiable in its delusion, does not know you — its own protector, the hero whose sole essence is compassion, who seeks the welfare [of all] for a long time. ||16||

children.text: bahudoṣo 'py ayaṃ lokaḥ sabhāgya iti me matiḥ |
children.translated_text: Though this world has many faults, it is fortunate — such is my view;

children.text: tvaṃ yasyaivaṃvidho nātha cirāt prabhṛticintakaḥ || 17
children.translated_text: for one such as you, O Protector, has been its long-standing benefactor. ||17||

children.translated_text: Who other than the Self-born (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>) ones could fully know your virtues —

children.text: guṇāṃs te nikhilaṃ ko 'nyaḥ svayaṃbhūbhyo 'vabhotsyate || 18
children.translated_text: [you] of extended resolve and renowned wondrous deeds? ||18||

children.text: tiṣṭhantv anye guṇās tāvat tava sarvaguṇākara |
children.translated_text: Let your other virtues stand aside for now, O treasury of all virtues;

children.text: yad asmadarthe khinno 'si tena pūjyo 'si no 'dhi[kam] || 19
children.translated_text: by the fact that you suffered for our sake, you are most worthy of our worship. ||19||

children.text: x x [cir]ātprabhṛty eva jāgarūkaṃ jagaddhite |

body.translated_text: Praise of the <s>Saṅgha</s> (<s>Saṅghastotrastava</s>) (Schlingloff 1955: 92-94, including the additions of Pauly in JA 1957: 292 ff.)

children.text: vasan veṇuvane śāstā saṃbuddho [dvipado]tt[a]m[a]ḥ |
children.translated_text: The Teacher, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Best of Bipeds, dwelling in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove),

children.text: purato bhikṣusaṃghasya [bhi]kṣasaṃgham avarṇayat || 1
children.translated_text: praised the community of monks before the assembly of monks. ||1||

children.text: a
children.translated_text: Endowed with infinite virtues, a treasury of the virtues of the jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: nantaguṇa[saṃ]pannaḥ saṃgharatnaguṇākaraḥ |
dvipā[da]cārisaṃkṣetraḥ satkṛto nṛsurāsuraiḥ || 2
children.translated_text: the best field among those who walk on two feet — honored by humans, gods, and <s>Asuras</s>. ||2||

children.text: puṇyakṣetram ayaṃ saṃghaḥ kleśakakṣasamuddhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: This <s>Saṅgha</s> is a field of merit, from which the thicket of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) has been uprooted;

children.text: vipākaphalavistīrṇo dakṣiṇīyo hy anuttaraḥ || 3
children.translated_text: vast in its fruit of ripening, worthy of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇīya</s>), unsurpassed. ||3||

children.text: śraddhābalena śīlena śrutatyāgabalena ca |
children.translated_text: With the power of faith, with morality, with the power of learning and generosity,

children.text: hrīravatrāpyasaṃpannā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 4
children.translated_text: endowed with moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>apatrāpya</s>) — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||4||

children.text: arthajñāś cārthakuśalāḥ kathikāś ca viśāradāḥ |
children.translated_text: Knowers of meaning, skilled in the import [of <s>Dharma</s>], eloquent speakers, confident —

children.text: muktā medhāvinaś caiva iha saṃghe vasanti te || 5
children.translated_text: liberated and wise — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||5||

children.text: śraddhādhanena śīlena śrutaty[āga]dh[ane]na ca |
children.translated_text: Endowed with the wealth of faith, with morality, with the wealth of learning and generosity,

children.text: prajñādhanena saṃpannā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 6
children.translated_text: endowed with the wealth of wisdom — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||6||

children.text: āraṇyakā bhikṣākāmā al[pe]c[ch]āḥ pāṃsukū[li]kāḥ |
children.translated_text: Forest-dwellers, fond of alms, of few desires, wearers of rag-robes,

children.text: paiṇḍapātikasaṃtuṣṭā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 7
children.translated_text: content with the alms-round — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||7||

children.text: saptakṛtvabhava x x [ga]tvā trir devamānuṣe |
children.translated_text: Those who return [at most] seven times, having gone [...] three times through divine and human [births],

children.text: prahīṇapañcasaṃkleśā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 8
children.translated_text: having abandoned the five afflictions — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||8||

children.text: bahuśrutāḥ śīlavantaḥ apramā[davi]hāriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Learned, virtuous, dwelling in heedfulness,

children.text: vimokṣadhyānasaṃpannā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 9
children.translated_text: accomplished in the liberations and <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||9||

children.text: catvāraś pratipannāś ca catvāraś ca phale sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Four on the path (<s>pratipanna</s>) and four established in the fruit (<s>phala</s>),

children.text: śaikṣāśaikṣā susaṃbuddhāḥ iha saṃghe vasanti te || 10
children.translated_text: learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and adepts (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), well-awakened — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||10||

children.text: abhidharmaś ca sūtre ca vinayaś ca x x x x |
children.translated_text: In <s>Abhidharma</s>, in <s>Sūtra</s>, and in <s>Vinaya</s> [...]

children.text: x x x x pratipannā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 11
children.translated_text: [...] practiced — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||11||

children.text: x x x [bhā]vanāmārgāḥ prajñāśīlasamāhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: [...] the paths of meditation, concentrated in wisdom and morality,

children.text: traidhātusamatikrāntā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 12
children.translated_text: having transcended the three realms (<s>traidhātu</s>) — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||12||

children.text: kāruṇā x x x maitrī yeṣāṃ sattveṣu bhāvitā |
children.translated_text: Compassionate [...] loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) cultivated toward beings,

children.text: hitānukampī sattveṣu iha saṃghe vasanti te || 13
children.translated_text: with beneficent sympathy toward beings — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||13||

children.text: smṛtyupasthānasampannā ṛddhipādasamanvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Accomplished in the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), endowed with the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>),

children.text: samyakprahāṇasaṃyuktā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 14
children.translated_text: united with the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||14||

children.text: indriyabalabodhyaṅgaṃ sadā samyaksubhāṣitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) — always well-spoken,

children.text: āryaṃ cāṣṭāṅgikaṃ mārgam iha saṃghe vasanti te || 15
children.translated_text: and the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>) — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||15||

children.text: ṣaḍabhijñam anuprāptāḥ pratisaṃvidāsaṃyutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having attained the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), endowed with the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>),

children.text: mahānubhāvā ye 'rhantaḥ iha saṃghe vasanti te || 16
children.translated_text: the <s>Arhats</s> of great power — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||16||

children.text: kampayanti mahīṃ x x sasamudrasaparvatām |
children.translated_text: They shake the great earth [...] with its oceans and mountains;

children.text: lābhinaḥ pra x x x x iha saṃghe vasanti te || 17
children.translated_text: gainers of [...] — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||17||

body.text:
maharddhikā ṛddhimantaḥ svacittavaśavartinaḥ |
  spṛśantaḥ śaśinaṃ sūryam iha saṃghe vasanti te || 17/18
body.translated_text: Of great supernatural power, possessing <s>ṛddhi</s>, masters of their own minds, touching the moon and sun — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||17/18||

body.text:
dānaṃ śīlaṃ mahākṣāntiṃ vīryam dhyānaṃ tathaiva ca |
  prajñāpāramitāḥ prāptā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 18/19
body.translated_text: Generosity, morality, great patience, vigor, meditation, and likewise the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) — those who have attained them dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||18/19||

body.text:
bodhipākṣikadharmā ye saptatriṃśad udāhṛtāḥ |
  ye samānaya vartanta iha saṃghe vasanti te || 19/20
body.translated_text: The thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipākṣika</s>) that are declared — those who live in accordance with them dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||19/20||

body.text:
Pauly: bodhipakṣikadharmā ye saptatriṃśad subhāvitāḥ |
  ye samādāya vartanta iha saṃghe vasanti te || 19/20
body.translated_text: [Pauly reading:] The thirty-seven <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening, well cultivated — those who live having undertaken them dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||19/20||

body.text:
prajñāvimuktās traividyāḥ ṣaḍabhijñā maharddhikāḥ |
  tribodhiprasthitāś cāryā iha saṃghe vasanti te || 20/21
body.translated_text: Liberated through wisdom, possessing the threefold knowledge (<s>traividya</s>), with the six superknowledges and great power, noble ones set forth toward the three awakenings — they dwell in this <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||20/21||

body.text:
stutva stutiśataiḥ stotraḥ saṃgharatnaṃ maharṣiṇā |
  atha sarvajagannāthaḥ punar attamano 'bravīt || 21/22
Pauly in d: punar uttaram abravīt
body.translated_text: Having praised the jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s> with hundreds of praises, the great Sage, the Protector of the entire world, with a pleased mind spoke again: ||21/22|| [Pauly reads in d: spoke further]

body.text:
nāsti buddhasamo śāstā nāsti dharmasamo dhvajaḥ |
  nāsti saṃghasamaṃ kṣetraṃ tasmāt saṃghe prasīdata || 22/23
body.translated_text: There is no teacher equal to the <s>Buddha</s>; there is no banner equal to the <s>Dharma</s>; there is no field equal to the <s>Saṅgha</s> — therefore, be devoted to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. ||22/23||
The Praise of the <s>Saṅgha</s> (<s>Saṅghastotrastava</s>) is complete.

children.text: prakāśitaṃ dharmavaraṃ praṇītaṃ
children.translated_text: The excellent <s>Dharma</s> has been proclaimed, sublime,

children.text: sudurdṛśaṃ śāntikaraṃ prajāyai |
children.translated_text: very difficult to see, bringing peace to beings — |

children.text: niryāṇikaṃ sarvaduḥkhakṣayāya
children.translated_text: leading to liberation, for the destruction of all suffering,

children.text: svayambhuvijñānabalair upetam || 1
children.translated_text: endowed with the powers of the self-born one's wisdom. || 1

body.translated_text: 1. metre: <s>Upajāti</s>

children.text: taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā vyapanītakāṃkṣāś
children.translated_text: Having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, with doubts removed,

children.text: caranti vidvā satatāpramattāḥ |
children.translated_text: the wise ones practice, always vigilant — |

children.text: nyāyābhiyuktāḥ sugatasya vākye
children.translated_text: devoted to propriety in the word of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: labhanti mokṣaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca nālpam || 2
children.translated_text: they attain liberation and no small happiness. || 2

children.text: na sarvavidyā na dhanaṃ na bhaiṣajyā
children.translated_text: Not all learning, not wealth, not medicines —

children.text: nyāyābhiyuktā vyapanenti duḥkham |
children.translated_text: devoted to propriety, they do not remove suffering — |

children.text: yathāryadharmaḥ paramarṣideśito
children.translated_text: as does the noble <s>Dharma</s> taught by the supreme sage:

children.text: nyāyābhiyogo vyapaneti nirjvaraḥ || 3
children.translated_text: devotion to propriety removes [suffering], free from fever. || 3

children.text: ratnākaraṃ dharmaṃ imaṃ vigāhya
children.translated_text: Having plunged into this jewel-mine of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: labhanti bodhyaṅgabalendriyāṇi |
children.translated_text: they obtain the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), powers, and faculties — |

children.text: te labdhalābhāḥ sukhitā aśokāḥ
children.translated_text: those who have gained attainment are happy, free from sorrow,

children.text: suniḥsṛtāḥ sarvabhavair vimuktāḥ || 4
children.translated_text: well-liberated, freed from all existences. || 4

children.text: sudurlabhaḥ kalpaśatair anekair
children.translated_text: Exceedingly difficult to obtain over countless hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: dharmo yaḥ svākhyāto jinapraśataḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s> well-proclaimed, praised by the <s>Jina</s> — |

children.text: taṃ prāpya dharmaṃ hy amṛtaṃ variṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: having attained that <s>Dharma</s>, the immortal, the supreme,

children.text: careta vidvā satatāpramattāḥ || 5
children.translated_text: practice, O wise ones, always vigilant! || 5

children.text: bahupretasahasrāṇām annpānaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: for many thousands of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), no food or drink is found. ||

children.translated_text: abandoning human bodies, they attend upon divine bodies. ||
